title: Residency-aware audit pipeline and WORM evidence handoff
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Build a residency-aware audit evidence pipeline that enforces retention policies and deposits tamper-evident WORM objects in-region. The service will convert admin actions, access records, and config changes into a signed evidence envelope, store the envelope in an immutable store per customer residency rules, and produce automated compliance bundles for auditors. The scope includes manifest format, KMS signing/attestation, retention enforcement, and an automated daily reporting job that assembles evidence summaries and delivery receipts.
background: Current audit logs are scattered across services and short-retention S3 buckets with manual export for compliance requests. Customers requiring in-region, immutable evidence and auditable retention enforcement have to rely on ad-hoc scripts. We need a deterministic, testable pipeline that guarantees non-rewritable retention (WORM semantics), region residency, and automated evidence reporting tied to our console and compliance workflows.
goals: Produce a standard evidence envelope (SOBJ) that contains raw log slices, index metadata, and a signed manifest
Store envelopes in region-specific immutable buckets/containers with enforced retention TTLs
Provide cryptographic integrity checks (rolling SHA-256 manifests + signature) and KMS-backed signing
Expose an API for auditors/seeded SRE to request compliance bundles and check evidence receipts
Automate daily/weekly evidence reports and receipts that are archived with retention metadata
non_goals: Re-architecting all existing log producers — we will focus on a shim/adapter layer
Public blockchain anchoring for every envelope (out of scope for MVP)
Customer-managed object storage for MVP — platform-managed in-region stores only
success_metrics: End-to-end sealed evidence for admin actions within the configured retention window: 99.9%
Evidence retrieval latency for a 90-day bundle: < 2 minutes (median)
Automated report generation success rate: > 99% per day
Security review and KMS attestation completed and approved
acceptance_criteria: Given an admin API action, the pipeline emits an evidence envelope and returns a delivery receipt with signed manifest
The envelope is written to an in-region immutable container with retention TTL enforced by storage-layer policy
Manifest contains SHA-256 checksums for each component and a platform KMS signature; optional customer KMS signature when provided
Automated daily reporter attaches a human-readable summary to the customer console and stores the canonical copy in the WORM store
Integration tests validate inability to overwrite or delete envelopes before retention expiry (simulated)
design_decisions: Use a small wrapper 'audit-shim' library for log producers to create canonical records rather than changing all services
Evidence envelope (SOBJ) format: JSON lines payload + compressed attachments + manifest metadata. Chosen for simplicity and streaming write semantics.
KMS signing: platform master key signs the manifest. If customer KMS key is available (Private mode), sign with both keys and store key fingerprint in manifest.
Retention enforcement implemented at storage policy level using provider immutable policies when available; otherwise we emulate via write-once + periodic attestation jobs.
Residency mapping will be driven by customer profile: region tag on envelope determines target WORM container
implementation_plan: Phase 1: PoC (2 weeks) - audit-shim + SOBJ format + local file-backed WORM emulator
Phase 2: Storage integration (3 weeks) - S3 Object Lock + provider-immutable containers for EU/US/APAC mapping
Phase 3: KMS signing and manifest schema (2 weeks) - integrate platform KMS, sign/verify logic
Phase 4: Retention enforcer and attestation job (2 weeks) - periodic verify and tamper report
Phase 5: Reporting automation and console hook (2 weeks) - daily bundle generator and console attachment
Phase 6: Hardening and tests (2 weeks) - e2e tests, chaos + residency failure cases, SLO dashboards
